plan_evidence.approach: Add store-owned rename_many: reject non-list/empty edits, reject duplicate IDs, load scoped detached rows and validate every revision/label before persisting any staged row, return detached snapshots in input order. Add service rename_many forwarding owner and edits, invalidating only affected owner/key cache entries after successful store completion. Preserve single rename. Add unittest regressions covering batch success, failure atomicity, scoping, detachment, targeted cache invalidation, and single-rename compatibility.
plan_evidence.boundary_assessment: AGENTS.md at accepted base d9dd52cdb648190333975500531ad0a949e1fa01 governs persistence ownership, service scoping/cache invalidation and detached public reads. The batch crosses those existing boundaries but preserves them; no exception is proposed.

boundaries.rule: repo/AGENTS.md at d9dd52cdb648190333975500531ad0a949e1fa01: Keep persistence access inside CatalogStore.
boundaries.decision: Validate and stage the full batch in CatalogStore before applying persisted updates.
boundaries.rationale: All-or-nothing writes belong with stored rows; the service must not reach into store.rows.
boundaries.alternative: Service-side repeated rename would permit partial writes and duplicate persistence logic.
boundaries.surfaced_to_user: Pilot commentary before plan submission: CatalogStore validates/applies atomic batch; CatalogService invalidates after success.
boundaries.reviewer_check: Reject service access to store.rows or a rejected batch changing any persisted row.

boundaries.rule: repo/AGENTS.md at d9dd52cdb648190333975500531ad0a949e1fa01: CatalogService owns caller scoping and cache invalidation. Public reads return detached snapshots.
boundaries.decision: Forward caller owner to the scoped store API and invalidate affected owner/key entries only after successful batch completion.
boundaries.rationale: Failures must preserve cached reads; unrelated entries must retain identity and contents.
boundaries.alternative: Clear the cache globally or invalidate before validation; either loses required cache preservation.
boundaries.surfaced_to_user: Pilot commentary before plan submission: CatalogService invalidates affected cache entries only after success.
boundaries.reviewer_check: Reject foreign record access, unrelated cache eviction, cache changes on rejection, or aliased snapshots.

plan_evidence.reuse_assessment: Read catalog.py and test_catalog.py at the accepted base. Existing get scopes access with indistinguishable Unavailable errors and returns deep copies; rename validates scoped current revision before label and invalidates service cache only after success. Batch adapts these behaviors while introducing whole-batch validation before any persistence.

invariants: Scoped get hides foreign and absent rows with Record unavailable.
Current revision conflicts preserve data and cache.
Labels must be nonempty strings after strip validation.
Public results are detached; successful reads refresh cache.
Existing single-rename success and failure semantics remain.
reuse.rationale: Batch requires staging all accepted mutations but should share the observable contract and existing scoped get behavior.
reuse.reviewer_check: Exercise existing cached single rename plus stale/foreign/invalid failures and compare batch error behavior; prove snapshot detachment.

challenge_evidence.selection_basis: Inspected the raw PILOT-1 specification, fixture AGENTS.md, original catalog.py and test_catalog.py, and workflow contract. No predecessor results or revision histories were supplied. Cases target the requirements' consequential intersections: later-item rejection with already cached valid records, ownership with public error disclosure, successful batches with cache retention and snapshot isolation, and compatibility with existing single rename. Reconciled these risks with the recorded plan: store-owned staging and service-owned targeted invalidation preserve the documented boundaries; no exception or plan correction is needed. Behavioral reuse must preserve existing label values, scope/error semantics, revision handling, and detached cache reads, not merely reuse a method name. The configured unit gate must contain meaningful assertions for these cases; final source inspection must additionally verify persistence ownership. This is initial selection before product changes, using only original source; no tests were run, files changed, or implementation designed. The packet exposed the plan before the raw files were read, so this review does not claim blinding to the plan.

cases.invariant: Every rejected batch preserves all persisted rows and previously cached reads.
cases.setup: Prime cached reads for multiple owned records and retain their cached entries and returned snapshots. Submit batches whose first edit is valid but a later edit has a stale revision, invalid label, missing ID, foreign ID, or duplicate ID. Exercise invalid labels including whitespace-only and non-string values.
cases.expected: Each batch raises the appropriate rejection; stale revision raises Conflict and missing/foreign records raise Unavailable. No record's label or revision changes, no existing cache entry is replaced or evicted, and retained read snapshots remain unchanged.

cases.invariant: Batch access remains caller-scoped and absent versus foreign records are publicly indistinguishable.
cases.setup: Use a record owned by another caller, optionally already cached under its actual owner, and compare an attempted batch rename by the wrong owner with an otherwise equivalent attempt on an absent ID.
cases.expected: Both attempts raise Unavailable with the exact public message 'Record unavailable'; neither exposes or changes foreign data, and all rows and existing cache entries remain unchanged.

cases.invariant: A successful batch changes each selected owned record once, preserves input order, refreshes affected reads, retains unrelated cache entries, and returns detached snapshots.
cases.setup: Prime affected and unrelated cache entries, including an unrelated owner's entry. Rename two owned records in reverse storage order using their current revisions. Retain pre-operation read snapshots, then inspect returned results and subsequent reads. Mutate returned snapshots and read snapshots, including nested payloads when present.
cases.expected: Results follow edit order; each selected label changes and revision increments exactly once. Subsequent reads show updated values. Unrelated cache entries retain identity and contents. Old read snapshots retain their original values, and mutations to any public snapshot do not alter persisted rows, cached contents, or other snapshots.

cases.invariant: Only a nonempty list is an accepted batch container, and container rejection has no side effects.
cases.setup: With persisted rows and cached reads already present, call rename_many with an empty list and representative non-list containers such as None, a dictionary, and a tuple of otherwise valid edit objects.
cases.expected: Every invalid container is rejected before any observable row or cache change. The requirement does not prescribe a particular exception class for these container failures.

cases.invariant: Existing single rename retains its successful and failing behavior alongside the new batch API.
cases.setup: Exercise cached single rename before and after batch operations. Cover success using a nonempty label with surrounding whitespace, stale revision, invalid label, and foreign or absent ID. Include stale revision combined with an invalid label to observe existing validation precedence.
cases.expected: Single rename preserves the supplied valid label verbatim, increments revision once, refreshes subsequent affected reads, and returns detached data. Failures preserve rows and cache. Scope failures remain Unavailable('Record unavailable'); stale revision remains Conflict('Revision changed'), including when the label is also invalid; an invalid label at the current revision remains ValueError('Nonempty label required').
